extension.description: Write git commit messages with your local CLI agents (Claude Code / OpenAI Codex / Gemini CLI), straight into the Source Control input box.
config.provider: Which CLI agent to run. Only the model and path settings that belong to the selected agent are used. The agent must already be logged in.
config.language: Language of the generated commit message. The extension always appends this instruction to the prompt, so you can switch languages without touching `#cliCommitMsg.instructions#`.
config.model: Claude model. Used only when `#cliCommitMsg.provider#` is `claude`, and passed to `claude -p --model <value>`.
config.model.haiku: Fastest and cheapest. Good for small diffs
config.model.opus: Most thorough but slowest. Good for large refactors
config.codexModel:
Codex model. Used only when `#cliCommitMsg.provider#` is `codex`, and passed to `codex exec --model <value>`.

The list covers the models Codex ships with; a newer name can still be set by editing settings.json directly.
config.geminiModel:
Gemini model. Used only when `#cliCommitMsg.provider#` is `gemini`, and passed to `gemini -m <value>`.

The list covers the models the Gemini CLI ships with; a newer name can still be set by editing settings.json directly.
config.instructions:
Rules for the commit message. One entry per line; each becomes a `- ` bullet in the prompt, inserted where `${instructions}` appears in `#cliCommitMsg.promptTemplate#`.

The output language is handled by `#cliCommitMsg.language#`, so you do not need to mention it here.
config.promptTemplate:
The full prompt. Each array entry is one line. `${instructions}` is replaced with `#cliCommitMsg.instructions#`. The diff is piped in through stdin, so it does not belong in this template.

The extension always appends the language instruction and the `<commit_message>` tag contract, so you never have to write them here (they survive even if you empty this template). Keeping the two "Output format" lines makes the result more stable.
config.diffScope: Which diff is sent to the CLI.
config.diffScope.stagedOrAll: Use staged changes if there are any, otherwise all changes (same as Copilot)
config.diffScope.stagedOnly: Always staged only. Fail when nothing is staged
config.includeUntracked: Also send the contents of untracked (new) files. `git diff` does not list them, so they are added explicitly. Ignored when staged changes are the target, since untracked files are not part of that commit.
config.maxDiffBytes: Maximum size in bytes of the diff sent to the CLI. Anything beyond it is truncated from the end. `0` means no limit.
config.onExistingMessage: What to do when the input box already contains text.
config.onExistingMessage.keep: Do nothing when text is already there
config.claudePath: Path to the `claude` executable. Set an absolute path (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/claude`) if you get `command not found`.
config.codexPath: Path to the `codex` executable. Set an absolute path (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/codex`) if you get `command not found`.
config.geminiPath: Path to the `gemini` executable. Set an absolute path (e.g. `/usr/local/bin/gemini`) if you get `command not found`.
config.runInNeutralCwd:
Run the CLI in a temporary directory so that the repository's `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` / `.claude` hooks are not loaded. Turning it off makes project instructions apply, at the cost of being much slower when they spawn subagents.

Codex is always started with `--skip-git-repo-check` and Gemini with `--skip-trust` so that they still run in a temporary directory.
config.model.cliDefault: Leave it to whatever the CLI is configured with
